gui._comment_stepDirs: Folders holding the component STEP models, searched IN ORDER - the first one that holds a given model file wins. So a project-local folder listed above the shared library overrides individual models. Each folder is searched recursively, so subfolders need no entry of their own. Edit here or in the GUI, one folder per line.
gui._comment_silkscreenFlatHeight: Distance in mm from the board surface to the surface of a FLAT silkscreen, so that graphics do not flicker where the two would otherwise be coplanar. Not the ink thickness - that is settings.silkscreenThickness, and it applies to solid silkscreen only. 1 um is invisible at board scale; raise it to 0.005-0.01 if a particular viewer still flickers. Ignored when silkscreenFlat is false.
gui._comment_silkscreenLayersOff: Silkscreen layers left out of the build, by name, as ticked in the GUI's Silkscreen layers panel. Exclusions rather than inclusions on purpose: a layer that turns up on a board for the first time is drawn, instead of going missing with nothing on screen to say why. Empty means every collected layer is built.
gui._comment_windowGeometry: Where the window was when it was last closed, as Tk's WIDTHxHEIGHT+X+Y. Restored on the next run, so on a multi-monitor desk it comes back on the same screen (X may be negative for a monitor left of the primary). If the position is no longer reachable - typically the monitor it was on has been disconnected - it is ignored and the window is centred on the main screen instead. Delete this key to get the centred first-run placement back. windowState remembers whether it was maximized.
gui._comment_ignoreSoldermask: Leave the soldermask out of the board entirely, however the design defines it, and close the stack up toward the core by exactly the thickness removed - on each side independently. Components then rest on the copper rather than on the mask, and the board is that much thinner. Applies both to a multi-stackup board's layers and to a plain board's soldermask_top/soldermask_bottom. The GUI checkbox is 'Ignore soldermask layers'; the decision is made when the model is built, so it needs no re-export.
gui._comment_boardMode: How the board body is built on a MULTI-STACKUP / rigid-flex design; ignored on an ordinary board. 'solid' - one solid in one color, coplanar faces merged, smallest file. 'layers' - one solid whose layer interfaces are kept so every face can be colored by the kind of layer it belongs to and the rim shows the stack; about 4.7x the size of 'solid'. 'inspect' - every layer of every zone as its own named part, for taking the board apart by eye; largest. The GUI calls this 'Board'.
gui._comment_layerColors: Color per kind of stackup layer, used by boardMode 'layers'. Defaults are Allegro's own material colors, taken from a board's 3DX_APPEARANCE, so the export looks like the same board does in Allegro's 3D canvas. Set from the swatch row in the GUI or by hand as #RRGGBB.

settings._comment_negativeLayers: Stackup layers whose drawn shapes are OPENINGS rather than material, matched case-insensitively as a prefix of the layer name. Coverlay, soldermask and pastemask are drawn this way by convention (IPC-2581): a shape on them marks where the sheet is ABSENT, so the material is the zone minus those shapes. Stiffener, adhesive and epoxy are the opposite - their shapes ARE the material. Allegro's negativeArtwork flag does not answer this (it is about film generation and reads nil on every layer), so the polarity is taken from layerFunction when the design carries one and from this list otherwise. Add a layer here if its bodies come out inverted in the layer inspection build.
